justification: Removes the SEPP secondary-dwelling fallback constants (450 m2 / 60 m2) from the satellite granny-flat service (#817), the last surface carrying the defect class removed from conveyancing in #684/#816. Regulatory figures in a paid product now come only from housing_sepp_standards; unavailable standards fail the endpoints closed (503). Above minor (regulatory figures, endpoint behaviour change); below critical (no new data source, query, or schema).

pre_impl.existing_data: housing_sepp_standards (migration 045) exists in production with min_lot_size and max_floor_area rows for secondary_dwelling, so the fallback only ever fired on DB-unreachable. The intelligence brief is decoupled from this service (light marker only), so the only consumers are the Next.js granny-flat routes, which already surface HTTP errors as visible failure states.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The response contracts (sepp_eligible bool, max_floor_area_m2 float) are consumed by six frontend files, so a three-state field change would ripple widely. Chose fail-closed 503 instead: when standards cannot be loaded neither endpoint can compute anything meaningful (eligibility, floor area, build cost, and yield all derive from them), and a 503 can never render a wrong figure. test_granny_flat_logic imported the fallback constant as a geometry-test bound; replaced with a local fixture constant.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: No new capability or contract change: same request and response models, same SQL. The change deletes the two constants, makes _get_sepp_sd_standards return None per missing standard, and adds a 503 guard at each endpoint after the existing load sites. Mirrors the #684 pattern one level up: conveyancing renders 'Not assessed' inside a multi-section report; a single-purpose API endpoint fails the request.

functions.name: _get_sepp_sd_standards
functions.input: optional psycopg2 connection to the production database, None when no connection could be opened
functions.output: tuple of min lot area and max floor area floats loaded from housing_sepp_standards rows
functions.if_none: conn None, query failure, or a missing row now yields None for that standard instead of substituting 450 or 60; callers fail closed with a 503

functions.name: detect_structures
functions.input: GrannyFlatDetectRequest with address, coordinates, prop_id and optional lot geometry and lot area
functions.output: GrannyFlatDetectResponse with sepp_eligible screen, detected structures, tile payload and detect_id
functions.if_none: sepp_min_lot None raises HTTPException 503 before any eligibility screen, so sepp_eligible can never be computed against a hardcoded minimum

functions.name: confirm_and_calculate
functions.input: GrannyFlatConfirmRequest with confirmed structure count, lot area, heritage and existing-dwelling flags
functions.output: GrannyFlatConfirmResponse with buildable verdict, max floor area, build cost, rent and confidence
functions.if_none: either standard None raises HTTPException 503, so buildable verdict, floor area cap, and cost figures can never derive from hardcoded defaults

values.value: min_lot_size and max_floor_area numeric_value rows from housing_sepp_standards for secondary_dwelling
values.read_at: services/granny_flat.py _get_sepp_sd_standards, per-key rows.get with no default
values.if_missing: None propagates to the endpoint guards which raise 503 with a message naming the SEPP as the source to consult; no figure renders

queries: N/A - the housing_sepp_standards SELECT (development_type + standard_type filter) is byte-identical to before; only the handling of missing rows changed.

break_it.scenario: Database unreachable when a user runs the granny-flat tool, which previously screened eligibility against the hardcoded 450 m2 and priced the build from the hardcoded 60 m2.
break_it.what_happens: A stale SEPP amendment would silently produce wrong eligibility verdicts and wrong cost figures in a paid product.
break_it.how: Both endpoints now raise 503 with a message naming the SEPP as the authoritative source; the frontend routes already render fetch failures visibly. test_detect_503_when_standards_unavailable and test_confirm_503_when_standards_unavailable pin this.
break_it.repro: Monkeypatch _get_sepp_sd_standards to return (None, None) and call either endpoint.

break_it.scenario: A half-loaded standards table, for example min_lot_size present but max_floor_area deleted, lets confirm price a build from a defaulted floor area.
break_it.what_happens: A real minimum mixed with an invented cap produces a cost and yield figure indistinguishable from a fully sourced one.
break_it.how: rows.get now has no default so the missing standard is None, and confirm requires both standards before proceeding. test_partial_db_values_none_for_missing and test_confirm_503_when_max_floor_area_missing pin both layers.
break_it.repro: Monkeypatch _get_sepp_sd_standards to return (450.0, None) and call confirm_and_calculate.

break_it.scenario: Someone reintroduces the constants during a refactor, restoring the silent fallback while all ordinary tests still pass because they inject standards.
break_it.what_happens: The defect class returns invisibly and only fires in production during a DB outage.
break_it.how: test_sepp_fallback_constants_never_return greps the service source for _SEPP_FALLBACK and hardcoded 450/60 default phrases; test_confirm_renders_injected_figures_not_constants injects 75 m2 and asserts it flows to the response and build cost.
break_it.repro: Re-add _SEPP_FALLBACK_MIN_LOT_M2 = 450.0 to granny_flat.py and run tests/test_granny_flat_mutation.py.

break_it.scenario: The 503 fires during a transient DB blip mid-flow: a user who completed the detect step gets an error on confirm and loses the run.
break_it.what_happens: Worse UX than the old silent fallback for that user, traded deliberately for never rendering an unverifiable figure.
break_it.how: Failure is loud and retryable: the detail message says to retry later, the detect flow can be re-run, and standards exist in production so this only occurs when the DB is down, when report writes and heritage checks are already degraded.
break_it.repro: Kill the DB connection between detect and confirm and observe a 503 with the retry message rather than a report with defaulted figures.

post_merge.db_reset: Not required - no schema or data changes; reads the existing housing_sepp_standards rows exactly as before.
post_merge.secrets: No secrets involved - connection handling unchanged.
post_merge.other_repo: None. This closes the defect class opened by #681/#684: no remaining SEPP/SD fallback constants in services, scripts, or src.
post_merge.manual_verify: Yes - with the DB reachable both endpoints behave identically to before (standards exist in prod); with DATABASE_URL broken, detect and confirm return 503 with the SEPP-naming message instead of a report containing 450/60 figures.
